column1: # redaction.tsv — the runlog kit's redaction table. One row per secret class, applied once on read.
# The columns, TAB-separated, follow the header row below.
#   id        one id of the closed class list the reader module declares. The self-test asserts
#             the table against that list in both directions, so a row cannot go missing quietly.
#   hint      one or more lowercase substrings joined by `|`. A rule's regex runs only on text whose
#             lowercased form holds at least one of them, which keeps most strings off the regex path.
#   pattern   a Python regex, compiled on its own so no rule's inline flags reach another. Its named
#             group `v` is the secret VALUE. What sits outside `v` is the key or prefix that names the
#             secret, and the render keeps it.
#   positive  a TEMPLATE the rule must redact, never a literal credential. `{A36}` is 36 random
#             alphanumerics, expanded by the self-test alone. The classes are A alphanumeric, U
#             uppercase or digit, L letter, a lowercase or digit, D digit, H hex, B base64 and S
#             URL-safe, and `{NL}` is a newline. At most 196 characters once expanded.
#   negative  a near miss the WHOLE table leaves unchanged, not only its own rule.
# Rules run in this order, and a span an earlier rule took is not matched again. The first rule to
# claim a positive must be that positive's own. No committed file of this kit carries text this table
# flags outside the positive column: the self-test scans the kit with the table to prove it, which is
# what keeps a public repository clear of push protection. A new class is one id in the reader
# module, one row here, and its positive and negative.
id
url-userinfo
auth-header
github-token
sk-key
aws-key
column5: the AKIAEXAMPLE prefix, and akia{U16} in lowercase
